title: A Microfluidic Model of Biomimetically Breathing Pulmonary Acinar Airways
protocol: Use deep reactive ion etching (DRIE) of a silicon on insulator (SOI) wafer to fabricate a master silicon wafer.
Mix PDMS and curing agent at a 10:1 weight ratio inside a clean small container such as a plastic weighing dish.
Degas the mixture in a desiccator under vacuum until all air bubbles are removed.
Pour the degassed-mixture to a height of approximately 1 mm above the master wafer.
Degas once again for at least 40 min to remove all the air bubbles above the wafer and minimize the bubbles below the wafer.
Bake at 65 °C for 20 min in a natural convection oven.
File the barrel section of a plastic 2 ml syringe using fine grit sandpaper to improve adherence to PDMS.
Use sandpaper to flatten the base of the syringe barrel by placing it on a flat surface and sliding.
Clean the syringe with pressurized air.
Place the barrel section of the syringe on top of the first PDMS layer with the large opening facing the PDMS surface.
Pour a second layer of PDMS around the barrel to a height of ~5 mm, avoiding entry into the barrel.
Degas the PDMS in a desiccator.
Bake the entire setup at 65°C for at least 2 hours in a natural convection oven.
Cut through the PDMS mold around the patterned region using a scalpel while lightly touching the surface of the master wafer.
Insert a thin tool such as wafer forceps into the notch created by the scalpel.
Peel off the PDMS cast from the master wafer.
Place the cast on a soft surface covered with aluminum foil with the patterned side facing up.
Punch a hole in the PDMS at the chamber inlet and channel inlet using a 1 mm biopsy punch.
Coat a clean glass slide with a degassed 10:1 PDMS:curing-agent mixture using a spin coater programmed at 3,000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Bake the coated slide for more than 1 hour at 65 °C.
Clean the slide and PDMS cast using clear tape.
Treat the surface of the PDMS mold and PDMS-coated glass slide with O2 plasma for 1 minute.
Press the surfaces together gently after oxygen plasma treatment.
Bake the assembly overnight at 65 °C.
Mix water-suspended fluorescent polystyrene particles with a 64/36 (v/v) glycerol/water mixture containing 0.25% (w/w) particles in a glass vial.
Place a drop of the glycerol solution on top of the channel inlet and a drop of DI water on the chamber inlet.
Place the apparatus inside a desiccator and evacuate for approximately 5 minutes.
Wait for bubbles in the drops to pop before releasing the vacuum.
Release the vacuum, allowing liquids to be sucked into the voids inside the device.
Apply external pressure using a syringe if residual air remains inside the channels to allow air diffusion into PDMS.
Inject approximately 2 ml of DI water into the top chamber until fully filled with water.
Cover the top chamber with a 19 gauge blunt syringe tip.
Cut the tip of another blunt 19 gauge syringe tip and insert it to the side chamber inlet.
Connect both syringe tips to a 1 ml syringe via thin Teflon tubing and a T-shaped connector.
Ensure that the 1 ml syringe, Teflon tubing, T-shaped connector, and top chamber are all filled with water without bubbles.
Reconnect connection points after pushing water through empty sections of tubing to remove air bubbles.

Connect the 1 ml syringe to a pre-programmed syringe pump mimicking a quiet tidal breathing cycle (period T = 4 sec) consisting of linear ramps from zero to 1.8 ml/min in 1 sec, from 1.8 ml/min to -1.8 ml/min in 2 sec, and from -1.8 ml/min back to zero in 1 sec.

Obtain a series of 9 to 12 phase-locked, double-frame images of the particle-seeded flow using a µPIV system consisting of a dual frame-multiple exposure CCD camera (e.g., 1600 × 1200 pixels), a double pulsed Nd-YAG laser (wavelength: 532 nm, output energy: 400 mJ, pulse duration: 4 nsec), and an inverted microscope while the device is being actuated.
Acquire double frame series at 10 Hz for phase-locked double frame images.
Reorganize data so that all frame pairs separated by one full cycle time form a new time series.
Modify the lag time between first and second frames in each pair from 100 µsec to 0.1 sec.
Compute phase-locked velocity vector maps of resulting flow field using sum-of-correlation algorithm.
Repeat process with varying lag times for resolving different flow regions inside alveolar cavity.
Stitch individual flow maps together into a complete, high-detailed map by averaging overlapping data points.
